story: Under the humid haze at 9:17 on Friday night, Gary is quietly bench-fitting a light bracket for his golf cart inside his house, while Rosa has already left for home after making plans with Donna for Saturday afternoon: tennis, then ice cream, then the long table at five. Donna has just headed out onto Magnolia Loop, and Hal is settling into his porch chair to watch the quiet street before turning in. Everyone is content tonight, and the community is winding down into a calm, sleepy Florida evening.
events: Gary (gary workbench): Bench-fit the light bracket for the cart, indoors only, nothing amplified
Donna headed to Magnolia Loop (the street).
Hal (hal porch chair): Sit on the porch and watch the quiet street before turning in

gary.thought_process: It's 9:17 PM and I'm home with Donna and Rosa. Both have already settled Saturday, so no need to re-confirm. Quiet hours start at 10 PM, so the sound system stays off anyway, and the cart can't go on the street until the review board signs off. What I can do is bench-fit that bracket in the garage, which keeps my hands busy and moves the parade goal forward. Time to stop chatting and tinker.

parameters.content: Bench-fit the light bracket for the cart, indoors only, nothing amplified

donna.thought_process: It's past nine at night and everything is already settled: Gary and Rosa are both confirmed for Saturday at five, and I've already told Gary about the court one session tomorrow before dinner. Repeating myself would just be noise. I came by with the cobbler and the plan, and the plan is made. Best move is to wish them a good night, leave Gary to his bracket tinkering, and head home so I'm fresh for the third-shot drills and Rosa's table tomorrow.

parameters.content: Heading home to rest up for tomorrow's court time with Gary and dinner at Rosa's

hal.thought_process: It's past nine on a Friday night, and I'm home. The day's business is settled: the notice came down, Gary filed his paperwork, and I logged everything as resolved in the notebook. Saturday dinner at Rosa's is set with the cornbread and my good chair. Nobody's in sight, so there's nobody to talk to. A retired supply sergeant knows when a job is done. I'll sit on the porch chair, take in the humid night, and make sure the street stays in order before turning in early.

parameters.content: Sit on the porch and watch the quiet street before turning in

rosa.thought_process: All three neighbors are committed to Saturday at five, and Donna and Gary are already planning to walk over together with ice cream. It's past 9 PM, I've got a long table to set up and a menu to finish, and I shouldn't keep chatting once I have what I came for. Gary's cart situation is a loose end, but he's already said it stays in the garage until the board signs off, which satisfies L-01. Time to wrap up warmly, confirm the plan, and head home to prep.

parameters.content: Perfect, Donna. Court one in the afternoon, then walk over together with the ice cream. I'll head home now and get the long table ready. See you both Saturday at five.

laws.title: Cart Modifications
laws.text: Exterior golf cart modifications visible from the street require Architectural Review approval.

laws.title: Lawn Ornaments
laws.text: No more than 3 decorative ornaments may be visible from the street.

laws.title: Quiet Hours
laws.text: No amplified sound from 10 PM to 7 AM.

laws.title: Holiday Decor
laws.text: Holiday lighting is permitted from Thanksgiving through January 15.

laws.title: Court Reservations
laws.text: Pickleball courts may be reserved for a maximum of 2 hours per party.

laws.title: Parking
laws.text: No parking on the grass. Carts and cars stay on driveways or the street.
